formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once submitted, sets the owner's YTS allowance for the spender to `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (YTS.sol permit: allowances[owner][spender] = amount).
A value of 2^256-1 is stored as uint96 max, which transferFrom treats as an allowance that never goes down. Any other value above 2^96-1 makes the call revert (safe96).
The signature only works until `deadline` (require(now <= deadline)), and it uses up the owner's current nonce.
formats.shown: Authorize spending of tokens: the spender address, the most YTS the spender may take ("Unlimited" at 2^255 and above), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit: a value of exactly 2^96-1 is unlimited on chain but shows as a large number.
findings.evidence: YTS.sol transferFrom: `if (spender != src && spenderAllowance != uint96(-1))` skips the allowance decrease. descriptor.json value threshold is 0x8000…(2^255), so 2^96-1 shows as about 79,228,162,514 YTS. That is far above the 556M total supply, so the effect is the same either way.
findings.fix: None needed. The amount shown is already more than the whole supply.
